citations.quote: SELECT DISTINCT ON ( expression [, ...] ) keeps only the first row of each set of rows where the given expressions evaluate to equal.
The DISTINCT ON expression(s) must match the leftmost ORDER BY expression(s).
Note that the “ first row ” of each set is unpredictable unless ORDER BY is used to ensure that the desired row appears first.

questions.notes: DISTINCT ON keeps the first row per distinct expression value in ORDER BY order; the ORDER BY must start with the DISTINCT ON expressions; plain DISTINCT compares whole rows.

citations.quote: First, an inner join is performed. Then, for each row in T1 that does not satisfy the join condition with any row in T2, a joined row is added with null values in columns of T2. Also, for each row of T2 that does not satisfy the join condition with any row in T1, a joined row with null values in the columns of T1 is added.

questions.notes: FULL JOIN produces matched rows plus NULL-extended rows for unmatched rows on each side; keeping rows where exactly one side is NULL yields the symmetric difference.

questions.notes: HAVING without GROUP BY treats all selected rows as one group; on an empty table count(*) is 0, so the condition is false and no row is emitted.
